notes.observation: 'மாணவ நேசன்' is Kalaignar's handwritten student periodical. The chapter explains its format, copying method, circulation and role in his development as a writer.

notes.translation_action: Retain the proverb as a compact image ('little drops make a great flood' or equivalent), not as an explanatory paraphrase about small efforts accumulating.

notes.observation: Kalaignar specifies 'டெம்மி பேப்பர்' costs and says 'உழைப்பும் கட்டுரைகளும் இனாம்!' while describing at least fifty handwritten copies, eight pages per issue, twice monthly.
notes.translation_action: Preserve the concrete production economics and joke: demy paper cost was collected, while labour and articles were free/gratis. Do not genericize this into 'printing expenses'.

notes.observation: The difficulty of handwriting fifty copies of 'மாணவ நேசன்' leads directly to the thought 'வேறு என்ன செய்யலாம்' and then to 'முரசொலி'—explicitly not first as a weekly or monthly but as 'துண்டு வெளியீடுகளாக!'
notes.translation_action: Preserve this origin sequence and the emphatic final fragment: Murasoli emerges from a practical copying problem and begins as leaflet/pamphlet issues, not as a conventional periodical.

notes.observation: The narrator says the khadi-shirted bespectacled organizer encountered him as a thin fifteen-year-old, then page 55 says this meeting occurred four months before Murasoli began. external_contextual_evidence.finding: Tamil lexical sources attest 'முடங்கல்' as a rolled-palm-leaf letter / letter, confirming that the page-51 word is meaningful archaic vocabulary rather than an OCR error.

Independent Dravidian-movement historical listings name Pattukkottai Alagirisami and C. P. Chittarasu separately alongside Periyar and Anna, supporting the contextual reading of the source's unpunctuated 'அழகிரி சிற்றரசு' sequence as two people.
Jawaharlal Nehru's own 1939 writings record his China trip and an early return after war broke out, corroborating the chapter's event identity without replacing Kalaignar's wording.

Biographical reference works place the Radical Democratic Party in 1940 and the League of Radical Congressmen in 1939; the memoir explicitly says 1939 for 'புரட்சி ஜனநாயகக் கட்சி', so the memoir's year is preserved as authored chronology.

Murasoli's official institutional history dates its first issue to 10 August 1942 and says Karunanidhi was eighteen; the memoir here pairs a fifteen-year-old self-description with a meeting said to be four months before Murasoli began. This is recorded as an authored timeline tension, not corrected in translation.
